items.b: MOUAWAD PARURE MAKES HKD 613,600 AT BONHAMS HONG KONG, 48.9% BELOW ITS HIGH ESTIMATE
items.t: A Mouawad ruby, emerald and diamond parure led Bonhams' Online Jewellery, Hong Kong sale of 2 September at HKD 613,600, or $78,277, against a HKD 1.2 million high estimate of $153,085. The four-piece suite carries roughly 254 carats of gem material: 75 of rubies, 140 of emeralds and 39 of diamonds. Every other named lot in Rapaport's report cleared inside its estimate, including a Burmese jadeite ring at HKD 281,600 and three separate lots that each made HKD 179,200. Bonhams published no sale total.

items.b: CIBJO BACKS 'SYNTHETIC' ALONE WHILE THE FTC KEEPS THREE TERMS UNTIL 2028
items.t: CIBJO's general assembly and board took up the switch to synthetic at the close of its centenary congress in Vicenza on 7 September, putting the confederation alongside the London Diamond Bourse and the African Diamond Producers Association. Its diamond commission began studying the change in 2025; its coloured stone commission voted the same way on 6 September. CIBJO's own Laboratory-Grown Diamond Steering Committee had asked to keep laboratory-grown as one alternative term. The US Federal Trade Commission still allows synthetic, lab-grown and lab-created under its 2018 guides, next revised in 2028. France and Russia allow synthetic only.

items.b: PLATINUM ADDS $6.00 TO $1,829.00 AS THE OTHER THREE METALS HOLD LOWER
items.t: On Kitco's bid at 10:04 UTC, platinum was the only one of four metals higher, at $1,829.00 against $1,823.00 on 7 September. Gold shed $6.00 to $4,399.10, the same figure in the opposite direction; silver eased $0.101 to $65.946 and palladium $3.00 to $1,371.00. The gold-silver ratio narrowed to 66.7 ounces from 67.1. Palladium's bid-ask spread stayed at 2.9176% of the bid, and it covered $71.00 on the session, the widest range of the four. No source read named a cause.

items.b: DMCC TOKENISES A 1,971KG SILVER BAR, ITS FIRST COMMODITY ASSET UNDER THE VARA FRAMEWORK
items.t: Tokinvest, regulated by Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, began issuing fractional digital interests in the bar on 7 September as an Asset-Referenced Virtual Asset on BNB Chain. Brink's holds the metal and DMCC Tradeflow registers it. SAM Precious Metals cast the bar in the UAE at 99.9% purity, sized to 1971, the year the country was founded, and it was unveiled at DMCC's Dubai Precious Metals Conference in November 2025. At 63,369 troy ounces and Kitco's $65.946 bid, the metal is worth about $4.18m. Regulated secondary trading opens after the issue.

items.b: CIBJO'S FIRST BLUE LIST DEFINES SUSTAINABLE, RESPONSIBLE AND ETHICAL
items.t: CIBJO's Jewellery Supply Chain Committee presented the first edition of the Blue List on the final day of the Vicenza congress, 7 September, naming the three words its lead Kele Mafole said confuse buyers most. Responsible is defined as meeting internationally recognised standards, one test. Ethical adds current best practice in social responsibilities, two tests. Sustainable names socioeconomic benefit, environmental protection and longevity, and points at no outside standard. CIBJO presents it as a guidance document, not a certification.

tape_ts: 8 Sep 2026 - Kitco, re-read by the Editor at press time, 10:04 UTC. All four metals had moved off the 05:00 mark, so all four are carried here at Kitco's bid as the paper's one price for the morning: gold 4,399.10, silver 65.946, platinum 1,829.00, palladium 1,371.00. Platinum was the only one higher, and Business Insider quoted it 0.246% away from Kitco's mid on the same read, inside the timing-noise band.
